figures.alt: White exterior door with an even sweep contact on a clean aluminum threshold
figures.caption: Inspect the sill, jambs, sweep, and floor before replacing a threshold. A new threshold cannot correct rot, a damaged subfloor, or a door that is out of square.
figures.before: When You Need a Permit in Jacksonville

figures.alt: Localized moisture-softened wood at the lower corner of an exterior door jamb
figures.caption: Fit the threshold to sound material, preserve its drainage slope, and seal the ends without trapping water. Soft jamb or sill material is a broader repair than simply changing the metal cap.

figures.alt: Exterior door with a dry, neatly sealed lower opening and intact jamb weatherstrip
figures.caption: Test the sweep, latch, and full water-shedding path with the door closed. Wind-driven rain should move outward across the stoop, not collect at the interior edge of the threshold.
